title: Operator Onboarding and Certification Pathway
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This page defines the formal onboarding and certification pathway for platform operators who will run, diagnose, and restore Redwood Inference platform services in production. The goal is to reduce time-to-competence, surface measurable readiness milestones, and ensure consistent operator handoffs across regional teams.

Scope:
- Applies to new and rotating platform operators in the Eng Platform team (primary owners).
- Covers core runtime services, tenant routing, KV/prefix cache operations, GPU pool maintenance, canary rollouts, and emergency model swap procedures.
- Does NOT replace team-level runbook ownership; it standardizes baseline skills and triage patterns.

Audience:
- Primary: Platform operators and SREs joining the Eng Platform team.
- Secondary: On-call engineers from Eng Serving Runtime, Eng Infra, and Customer Success who will be cross-trained.

Why this exists:
- Recent retrospectives found inconsistent operator responses across regions and a long tail of escalation for common KV-cache and model-swap operations. This pathway reduces cognitive overhead, improves mean-time-to-repair (MTTR), and makes staffing predictable.

Certification levels (three-tier model):
1) Operator I – Basic runtime competency (expected after 2 weeks).
   - Knowledge: Monitoring dashboards, alert interpretation, escalation flow.
   - Skills: Execute guarded runbook steps for standard incidents (eg. reclaiming a stuck worker, rolling back a canary).
   - Acceptance: Pass the Level 1 lab exercises and checklist.
2) Operator II – Intermediate (expected after 8–12 weeks).
   - Knowledge: Queue demultiplexing, prefix/KV cache shard rebalancing, tiered-degradation policy application.
   - Skills: Carry out controlled cache eviction, perform targeted tenant burst reallocation, run postmortem triage.
   - Acceptance: Complete Operator II practical exam and 2 supervised incident rotations.
3) Operator III – Senior operator and trainer (expected 6+ months).
   - Knowledge: Capacity forecasting heuristics, cost-signal actioning, cross-region failover orchestration.
   - Skills: Lead incident commanders, author and approve new operator runbooks, mentor junior operators.
   - Acceptance: Peer-reviewed certification, policy signoff from Platform leads.

Curriculum and modules (recommended sequence):
A. Foundations (day 0–7):
   - Orientation: team wiki tour, SLAs/SLOs, incident taxonomy.
   - Accounts & Access: request RBAC roles (see Access & prerequisites), read-only dashboards.
   - Observability primer: tokenized SLI dashboards, cost-attribution panels, alert triage flow.
B. Basic runbook practice (week 1–2):
   - Guided walk-through of 5 canonical runbooks: worker restart, canary rollback, degraded-sli mitigation, small-scale KV prefix eviction, tracing a tail-latency spike.
   - Short quizzes and checklist signoff.
C. Lab exercises (week 2–6): hands-on sandbox with synthetic tenants. See "Runbook labs" below.
D. Intermediate ops patterns (week 6–12):
   - Queue slicing, tenant throttling simulator, predictive-scale behavior.
   - Review of platform routing policies and fallback catalog.
E. Practical exam and supervised on-call rotations (weeks 10–16):
   - Two graded scenarios: a regional cache rebalance and an emergency model swap with token surge.

Runbook labs (hands-on exercises):
- Lab 1: Prefix cache shard reallocation (sandbox). Steps:
  1. Trigger a controlled shard imbalance using provided CLI (lab-sim cache-disrupt).
  2. Follow rebalancing runbook to migrate shards (validate latency and eviction rate).
  3. Measure before/after metrics: cache hit %, token latency p50/p95, cost delta.
  4. Submit lab report with screenshots and a brief remediation justification.
- Lab 2: Emergency model swap and graceful fallback. Steps:
  1. Simulate a model runtime crash using fault injector.
  2. Execute emergency model-swap runbook: rollback policy, routing to compatible variant, and validate response correctness for a sample prompt set.
  3. Record rollback time and any client-visible errors.
- Lab 3: Tenant burst and soft quota handling. Steps:
  1. Use tenant-sim to introduce a token surge for a medium-priority tenant.
  2. Apply soft-quota mitigation, observe fair-share behavior, and verify SLA impact.

Assessment and acceptance criteria:
- Written checks (pass/fail) for Foundations and Basic Runbooks.
- Practical scoring rubric for labs (competence, safety, metric validation, communication).
- Operator I: complete Foundations + Lab 1, pass written checks.
- Operator II: complete Labs 1–3, pass practical exam (>=80%) and complete 2 supervised shifts with incident clearances.
- Operator III: demonstrated leadership in 3 incidents, authored at least 1 runbook improvement, and peer review approval.

Onboarding timeline example (recommended):
- Week 0: HR/People Ops onboarding and access provisioning.
- Week 1: Foundations + read-only dashboards.
- Week 2: Basic runbook practice + Lab 1.
- Week 4: Lab 2 + initial shadowing on rotations.
- Week 8: Lab 3 + practical exam scheduling.
- Week 10–16: Supervised rotations and certification decision.

Access & prerequisites (step-by-step):
1) Request accounts and roles: create ticket with People Ops: template 'Operator Onboard Access v2'. Required roles: platform-operator-read, platform-operator-rtc, kv-admin-lab (sandbox).
2) Approvals required: immediate manager and Eng Platform lead.
3) VPN + MFA setup: follow infra Onboarding guide.
4) Sandbox allocation: request ephemeral tenant sandbox via infra self-service portal (48-hour window by default).

Safety controls and escalation boundaries:
- No operator trainee should execute live KV shard migrations unsupervised until Operator II signoff.
- Emergency model swaps in production require two-person confirmation: the acting operator and an on-call runtime engineer.
- Any stateful rollback that touches customer data must be coordinated with Customer Success and marked as a P0 change in the change-management tracker.

Maintenance and re-certification:
- Operators must re-certify annually for Operator II/III to ensure familiarity with new routing policies, pricing-triggered throttles, and quantization profiles.
- Re-certification consists of a focused practical exam and a documentation quiz on changes in the past 12 months.

Tools, dashboards, and CLI snippets (practice list):
- Dashboards: token-cost-attribution, regional-eviction-tracker, kv-prefix-heatmap, canary-health-lane.
- CLI examples (sandbox):
  - Rebalance: redwoodctl cache rebalance --shard S-23 --target-node node-7 --dry-run
  - Emergency swap: redwoodctl models swap --tenant T-1001 --from=variant-a --to=variant-b --confirm
  - Simulate tenant surge: tenant-sim burst --tenant T-1001 --rps 1200 --duration 600s

Owner ship and responsibilities:
- Eng Platform learning lead (owner): Maya Chen — maintains curriculum and scheduling.
- Eng Platform operations lead: Ravi Kapoor — approves certifications and supervised incident signoffs.
- Eng Serving Runtime: liaison to validate model-swap exercises.

Metrics we will track to measure program success:
- Median time to Operator I readiness (target: <= 2 weeks).
- MTTR for canonical incidents before and after certification ramp (target: 25% reduction vs baseline).
- Number of runbook edits initiated by certified operators (target: 1 edit/operator/year).
- On-call pager noise reduction for common alerts (target: 20% decline in noisy alerts within 6 months).

Continuous improvement cycle:
1. Quarterly retrospective with training cohort and reviewers.
2. Curriculum updates published as change notes on this page.
3. Runbook changes must be linked to lab exercises and regression tests in the training sandbox.

Appendix A — Sample Operator I checklist (compact):
- [ ] Read tokenized SLI dashboard overview.
- [ ] Complete read-only access verification.
- [ ] Execute worker restart runbook in sandbox.
- [ ] Pass Foundations quiz (>=80%).

Appendix B — Example grading rubric (practical):
- Safety and adherence to runbook: 40%
- Successful restoration and metric validation: 30%
- Communication and incident writeup quality: 20%
- Post-action suggested improvements: 10%

Appendix C — Frequently asked questions:
Q: How do I schedule a supervised shift?
A: Use the scheduling sheet in the team wiki (link in Related Pages) and ping the Ops rotation owner.

Q: Who signs off Operator II?
A: Ops lead (Ravi Kapoor) plus one peer reviewer from Eng Serving Runtime.

Revision history:
- 2026-01-15: Document created by Maya Chen.
- 2026-02-10: Added Lab 3 and clarified two-person confirmation for model swaps (reviewed by Ravi Kapoor).
- 2026-03-02: Published final rubric and schedule template (reviewed by Elena Ruiz).

End of document."
